section_plan.title: Virtual Control Groups and Data Reuse as Reduction
section_plan.thesis: Reusing historical control-animal data as virtual control groups (VCGs) converts abstract data reuse into concrete Reduction - roughly a quarter fewer control animals - and the infrastructure to do it already exists at scale. But the payoff is conditional: concordance with concurrent controls is endpoint-dependent, temporal and cross-laboratory drift can bias conclusions, and no regulator has yet accepted a VCG-based study, so the ethical dividend remains partly theoretical.

conflicts_to_present.nature: Degree of VCG-concurrent-control concordance: a liver-enzyme simulation reports high agreement (>=90% in 68.5% of comparisons) whereas a clinical-pathology review reports 31-49% of quantitative parameters non-reproducible when concurrent controls are replaced - the central VCG tradeoff.

Temporal stability of historical control data: a rasH2 tumour-incidence analysis argues for minimal drift over a decade, while a multi-company clinical-pathology database finds study year is the single most influential covariate - determines whether pooled control data can be trusted.

Adequacy of historical control data for carcinogenicity conclusions: the Ramazzini Institute relies on its own and NTP historical controls to support treatment-related tumour findings, whereas EFSA rejected such conclusions partly because the historical controls were decades out of date and lacked a concurrent control.

section_plan.connection_prev: sec-fair-preclinical showed generic sharing rarely produces reuse; this section presents the clearest counter-case, where reusing a specific, well-curated data type (control-animal data) yields a measurable Reduction dividend, while inheriting the same data-quality and drift problems.
section_plan.connection_next: VCGs reuse animal data to reduce animal use; sec-nams-data addresses the complementary strategy - replacing animals with non-animal methods - and shows those methods generate their own data that must be stewarded to avoid re-incurring the debt.

figure_specs.label: fig:sec05-vcg-reduction
figure_specs.argument_supported: Quantifies the Reduction dividend of virtual control groups and control-data borrowing, showing convergence on ~25% control-animal reduction plus a clinical analogue.
figure_specs.what_it_reveals: Convergence of three preclinical estimates on ~25% - alongside a clinical Bayesian-borrowing enrolment reduction - shows the reduction figure is stable across independent groups, making it a defensible planning number.
figure_specs.caption_draft: Figure 12. Estimated animal/enrolment reduction from virtual control groups and Bayesian control-borrowing. Preclinical proposals converge on ~25% control-animal reduction (StegerHartmann2020; Gurjanov2024b; Adedeji2024), while a device-trial Bayesian dynamic-borrowing design reduced enrolment from 2,386 to ~1,497 under congruence (Chiaruttini2025). Reusing control data operationalises Reduction. Preclinical (animal-count) and clinical (enrolment) reductions are distinguished by category colour.

figure_specs.label: fig:sec05-vcg-concordance
figure_specs.argument_supported: Presents the central VCG tradeoff - that reduction comes at an endpoint-dependent concordance cost - so the ethical dividend is real but not free.
figure_specs.what_it_reveals: Setting high overall agreement (82%, 68.5%) against high clinical-pathology non-reproducibility (31-49%) on one axis shows the tradeoff is endpoint-specific, not a single verdict for or against VCGs.
figure_specs.caption_draft: Figure 13. Concordance between virtual/omitted-concurrent-control analyses and true concurrent controls. Omitting the concurrent control confirmed 82% of significant NHP parameters (Mecklenburg2023) and VCGs reproduced rat liver-enzyme decisions with >=90% agreement in 68.5% of comparisons (DuchateauNguyen2026), yet 31-49% of quantitative clinical-pathology parameters were non-reproducible when VCGs replaced concurrent controls (Adedeji2024). Agreement (repayment colour) and non-reproducibility (debt colour) are plotted together to show the endpoint-dependent tradeoff.

figure_specs.label: fig:sec05-shared-control-scale
figure_specs.argument_supported: Establishes that the infrastructure for control-data reuse already exists at scale, so the bottleneck is acceptance and stewardship, not data volume.
figure_specs.what_it_reveals: A single summary of database scales (tens of thousands of animals/studies) makes concrete that reuse is a solved data-availability problem for this specific data type, unlike the general FAIR failure in sec-fair-preclinical.
figure_specs.caption_draft: Figure 14. Scale of shared preclinical control/nonclinical databases. Curated resources already hold control and toxicology data at scale: 10,896 rats across 106 studies in RITA (Deschl2002), >60,000 rats plus 1,300 dogs and 500 monkeys in eTRANSAFE (Moresis2024), 6,500 legacy studies from eTOX (Pognan2021), and >10,000 SEND datasets in the FDA CDER repository (Snyder2024). The reuse infrastructure exists; acceptance and stewardship are the bottleneck. A log scale is used because counts span orders of magnitude; exact values are labelled.

debt_loss_negative.meaning: Data waste, bias inflation, loss, non-reproducibility - the debt

font.family: Source Sans Pro (fallback: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif)

figure_style_guide.redundant_cues_note: Never encode meaning by hue alone. Pair every colour with a second channel: hatch/pattern fills for declared vs actual (open hatch vs solid), distinct markers (circle/triangle/square) on forest and line plots, direct value labels on every bar, and short text annotations naming the focal contrast. Palette is the Okabe-Ito colourblind-safe set; verify with a deuteranopia/protanopia simulation before export.

recurring_themes: The declared-versus-actual gap: across FAIR audits, incentive studies and governance evaluations, stated intent (data-availability statements, DMP compliance, sharing pledges) vastly exceeds usable reality; recurs in sec-fair-preclinical, sec-incentives and sec-governance.
Convergence on ~2% actual data availability as the empirical anchor of the whole review, replicated across specialties and methods.
Reuse as Reduction: reusing existing data (historical/virtual controls, shared datasets, NAM outputs) is framed throughout as a direct 3Rs Reduction dividend, not merely good data hygiene.

False-consensus risk: several field-defining figures (11%/25% industry irreproducibility, US$28B/year, '85% of research wasted') rest on non-transparent or modeled sources and are flagged wherever cited.
Enforcement beats endorsement: passive publication of guidelines rarely changes behaviour; mandated, checked requirements do - a thread from sec-data-welfare through sec-incentives to sec-governance.
The animal-welfare stake: every data-stewardship failure is repeatedly tied back to its cost in animal lives, keeping the ethical argument foregrounded over the purely technical one.

Method-dependence of headline numbers: the same phenomenon (publication rate, concordance, QRP prevalence, sharing trend) yields very different values by method, so juxtaposition rather than single figures is the analytical style.

terminology.ethical_debt: The obligation incurred when animals are used to generate knowledge but the resulting data are allowed to become unfindable, unusable, or unreused; unpaid, it is discharged in further animal lives. Coined and used as the review's organising metaphor.
terminology.data_welfare: The claim that stewardship of animal-derived data (findability, reusability, complete reporting) is a dimension of animal welfare and of the 3Rs, because wasting the data wastes the welfare cost that produced it.
terminology.FAIR: Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable - the Wilkinson et al. (2016) principles for machine-actionable data stewardship. Distinguish FAIR (a stewardship standard) from 'open' (an access status); data can be FAIR without being fully open.
terminology.three_Rs: Replacement, Reduction, Refinement (Russell & Burch) - the ethical/legal framework for humane animal research. The review argues data welfare extends all three, chiefly Reduction and Refinement.
terminology.VCG: Virtual Control Group - a control arm reconstructed from curated historical control-animal data to partially or wholly replace concurrent controls, reducing control-animal use. Related term HCD = historical control data.
terminology.NAM: New Approach Methodology - non-animal methods (in silico/QSAR models, organoids, organ-on-chip/microphysiological systems, high-throughput screening) used to predict toxicity or biology; serve Replacement but generate data needing stewardship.
terminology.reproducibility_vs_replicability: Reproducibility = obtaining consistent results using the same data and analysis; replicability = obtaining consistent results in a new study with new data. The review uses 'reproducibility crisis' broadly but distinguishes the two where the evidence does (e.g., direct-replication projects test replicability; re-analysis disputes test reproducibility).
terminology.HBA: Harm-Benefit Analysis - the project-level weighing of animal harm against expected benefit that anchors animal-research regulation; its objectivity and predictive validity are contested.
terminology.QRP: Questionable Research Practice - selective reporting, p-hacking, undisclosed flexibility short of outright fabrication; a behavioural driver of the crisis.
terminology.ARRIVE: Animal Research: Reporting of In Vivo Experiments - the reporting guideline whose adherence and enforcement are evaluated in sec-governance.

cross_cutting_elements.voice_tone: Critical, evidence-anchored, and quantitative, but ethically serious rather than polemical. Foreground effect sizes and their provenance; state uncertainty and flag false-consensus risks explicitly rather than smoothing them over. Prefer juxtaposition of divergent estimates to single headline numbers. Keep the animal-welfare stake visible without moralising. Third person, present tense for findings; hedged claims ('the evidence suggests', 'audits converge on') proportional to evidence strength.
